text: Still can't believe they are releasing full-year data for Q3, but the "blackwell ramp" narrative has to be solidifying eventually. Even though I was hoping for a drop earlier, the fact that they beat EPS on revenue and the guidance continues to be so optimistic suggests the valuation might actually be a bit cheap compared to the trajectory. Just not watching the $800 range for a while...

Looks like another one of those reports where the stock goes up 20% after hours and stays flat all day. Honestly, at 500b revenue I'm just wondering if we are still selling GPUs to people who have the cash flow to pay for them. If Nvidia loses their moat to something like AMD or Xilinx, this 57b number means nothing. Did they actually fix their power supply issues or are they just selling us the same old silicon at a premium?

Honestly, the margin of error on a 30% revenue beat feels thin to me right now. I'm worried Jensen's Q4 guidance isn't fully backed by the production ramp numbers we actually see in the full 10Q. That 62% year-over-year is great, but does it account for the cost of goods sold and logistics we haven't seen yet? If Blackwell runs slow, we could be selling premium chips with lower volumes, which hurts margins. Also, with the cycle length so long, I don't think the 2026 numbers are a game-changer for valuation, but I do care if they actually execute the tech stack before the next cycle starts. Jensen is the only variable here who can tell us if the business will continue to scale, but right now the stock price feels like it's buying just the hope that the narrative holds, while the actual moat is still being carved out. Patience is key, and I'm not feeling any rush to get in unless the valuation starts to break.

"Wow, finally the full year is here and they didn't break any rules. I was just hoping Blackwell would actually ship before the holidays. With $57B revenue and that growth, I'm starting to see the actual value here rather than just the hype cycle. If Jensen can keep the guidance solid through Q4, maybe this is the endgame play I've been waiting for, though I'll take a small sell-off for now. 3 years left to see if this actually moves the needle."

Still have my eyes on the backflip, but honestly, that 62% beat isn't the whole story yet. With all that Blackwell ramp-up and the infrastructure demand narrative, I don't think the fundamental setup is as fragile as some of those "value trap" stories were. I'm willing to hold through the volatility and see if the next 5-year projection actually holds up, rather than trying to time the top off a single day's move.

I was so excited that I almost missed their quarterly call, but then I thought about where they're going next. If this 62% growth is the start of a real AI revolution where data center demand stays strong through 2028, they'll own the market for a decade. The Blackwell ramp looks solid and their engineering team seems to be doing what they should be doing for years. Great call by the CEO, but I'm mostly here for the long term, not the quarterly price swing.

As long as the supply chain holds up for data center production and we keep getting the Blackwell cards shipped, the rest of the story isn't going to matter until the next 5 year window opens up. Right now, the volatility is mostly just noise in a bull run that has really taken root.

I read the numbers and saw 62% growth, so I checked my 2022 portfolio. If we're looking at the long-term compounding of that scale here, I'm done with this quarterly noise and am just waiting to see where the next capex push lands. For now, the "wait and see" is already paid for.

Holy shit, that is actually insane. 62% YoY revenue and they beat? Just wow, the Blackwell ramp is going to be a real game changer here. Don't think the after-hours dip is a good sign otherwise; this momentum is just unreal right now. Long on the way up.

Holy shit. This is literally the first time in three years I've been watching a company in a bear market turn the tide this hard. Seeing the Blackwell ramp and that 62% Q3 beat? I'm finally thinking about buying the dip and holding here to ride the momentum before the AI sector goes sideways in Q4. Time to trade these things in the after-hours, don't touch the stock till the volume clears.

Yo, I'm actually kind of hoping the after-hours dump on the blackwell supply chain rumors is real. The stock just took a breather all week waiting for guidance, so if that Q4 guidance comes in a little soft on volume, I might just grab some dips before the retail volume starts to show up. Don't want to get swept in the hype cycle, though, so I'm watching this live.

Oof, the numbers are just as good as we're told and the stock is already at all-time highs today. If you think this is the top, you're right; but it feels like a wash if you're betting on a move higher. Next year we have to see if this momentum holds or if we just get baked by a year of all-time highs.

Okay holy cow, this is a historic run. 62% YoY on $57B is the kind of scale you only see in 30-year-olds. Jensen knows exactly what the AI market needs, so don't you dare mess with the tape right now. 🚀📈

Wait for the 4pm after-hours drop. $800 for 5.9% gain in Q2 was my main trade, and this 62% bump feels like a wash if we don't see NVIDIA in the 1000s soon. Let's see if Blackwell actually makes it through the delivery wave or if we just got caught in the hype train again.

Dank for the beat, but man, after-hours it was pure retail drama. 62% revenue up? That's insane for Q3 but the stock tanked until the open, then surged on the open. Classic flash crash. I'm still waiting for the momentum to catch up and the retail crowd to calm down; if they don't by noon tomorrow, I might be forced to cut my losses and buy the dips instead of holding the bag.
